rounds.text: Lloyds Engineering Works Ltd is riding exceptional operational momentum, evidenced by a massive 83% compounded sales growth over the trailing twelve months and a 64% compounded profit growth [E14, E15]. This top-line and bottom-line expansion is reinforced by robust fundamental returns, with a solid ROCE of 16.1% and ROE of 15.1% that outperform sector medians [E12, E13, E66]. The business benefits directly from a powerful macro environment, operating within a Capital Goods sector classified as a tailwind with a score of +0.59 [E61, E63]. Market participants are also recognizing this fundamental strength, as reflected by a high relative-strength rating of 88 against the Nifty 500 and a rules-based screen scoring a strong 82 out of 100 for a buy setup [E42, E53]. Furthermore, operational efficiency is visibly improving, highlighted by debtor days tightening significantly from 92.2 to 67.3 days alongside a healthy current ratio of 2.77x supporting short-term liquidity [E29, E51]. Conceded: [E36], which indicates that a discounted cash flow model calculates an intrinsic value of Rs 35 per share against the current market price.

Lloyds Engineering Works Ltd is currently trading at a significant valuation premium, with a P/E ratio of 60x [E1] and an EV/EBITDA of 45.84x, both of which vastly exceed their respective sector benchmarks [E6, E11]. This optimism is disconnected from the company’s fundamental performance, as evidenced by a discounted cash flow analysis that suggests an intrinsic value of only Rs 35 per share, implying a margin of safety of -145.8% [E36, E37]. The financial health of the firm is further strained by negative operating cash flow of Rs -253 Cr and free cash flow of Rs -494 Cr as of March 2026 [E26, E27]. Additionally, the company faces a concerning trend of declining promoter ownership, which has dropped from 59.79% in December 2023 to 40.00% in September 2026 [E32]. While the stock has shown strong price momentum, it carries high annualised volatility of 76.2% and a history of severe drawdowns reaching -92.1% [E44, E45]. Conceded: the company has demonstrated strong sales growth of 83% and profit growth of 64% over the trailing twelve months [E14, E15].

Conceded: [E1, E6, E11, E36, E37, E44, E45]. While the bear highlights rich valuation multiples and a DCF pointing to Rs 35 [E1, E36], the rules-based screen scores the company an 82 out of 100 with a BUY recommendation, driven by exceptional fundamental momentum [E53]. Conceded: [E26, E27]. The negative cash flows of March 2026 are accompanied by a massive 70.4% surge in Capital Work in Progress (CWIP) to Rs 121 Cr, proving that the negative cash burn is actually an aggressive growth and capacity build-up phase [E31]. Conceded: [E32]. Although promoter holding shifted, institutional confidence is surging with positive money flow and increased foreign and domestic holdings [E33, E34, E35]. Furthermore, the company operates within a powerful Capital Goods sector tailwind with a tailwind score of +0.59, while maintaining conservative debt-to-equity of 0.19x and a robust current ratio of 2.77x [E28, E29, E61].

Conceded: [E28, E29, E61]. While the bull points to a conservative debt-to-equity ratio of 0.19x and sector tailwinds, borrowings have quadrupled to Rs 445 Cr in September 2026 from Rs 109 Cr a year earlier [E30]. Conceded: [E33, E34, E35]. Despite institutional inflows, promoters have aggressively slashed their stake to 40.00% as of September 2026 from 59.79% in December 2023 [E32]. Conceded: [E31]. The defense that negative cash flow is merely aggressive capital expenditure ignores the severity of a negative free cash flow of Rs 494 Cr and negative operating cash flow of Rs 253 Cr in March 2026 [E26, E27]. Furthermore, relying on an 82 out of 100 rules-based screen [E53] disregards explicit warnings that earnings growth is decelerating and the DCF model signals an overvaluation of 146% [E58, E59].
